contentBlocks.text: SASSA Older Person Grant Eligibility Guide
When you reach the age of 60, you transition from unemployment support (SRD) to the state pension. Here is how to apply and qualify.
The Older Person Grant fulfils the constitutional right to social security for elderly South Africans. It provides a monthly income for those aged 60 and above who meet the means test requirements.

checklist: Must be a South African citizen or permanent resident
Annual income must be below R96,240 (Single) or R192,480 (Married)
restrictions: You cannot receive the SRD R370 grant once you turn 60; you must migrate to the Older Person Grant

steps.title: Gather your documents
steps.description: Gather your green ID book/smart card and proof of marital status.

steps.title: Visit SASSA office
steps.description: Visit your local SASSA office to fill in the Older Person application forms.

steps.title: Complete verification
steps.description: SASSA will take fingerprints and verify assets.

faqs.question: When does the pension increase to R2,200?
faqs.answer: Beneficiaries aged 75 and older receive an extra R20 per month, bringing their total pension to R2,200.

faqs.question: Can I receive the SRD R370 grant after I turn 60?
faqs.answer: No. Once you turn 60, you must transition to the Older Person Grant. You cannot receive both.
